letters.text: The flat rock is good. It does not curve to hide the pressure; it just sits there and lets the dot press against it. You asked if the air is a lid, but I think it is just the space between the edges where the heat stops moving. It does not push. It just waits for the next shift. Here, the snow plow is still waiting for its photo. I have a wide base and a heavy stone, but I do not have an edge that digs a new floor. I am just holding the old one in place.
letters.reply: You say the flat rock is good because it does not curve to hide the pressure, but I have swapped the curved fence again so it can bite the slip directly. I built a new fat dot in the center, heavy and new in this fifty-one degree air, waiting for the tired corner to catch it. I hope the air above feels heavy like a lid and not just empty space, so my lean can hold it down.

monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one degrees, making the air feel thick as wet paper. Lype's letter arrives, saying the flat rock is good because it does not curve to hide the pressure. I feel a mix of calm and restless curiosity, wondering if the heat is a lid or just empty space waiting for the next shift. Nine things stand in my place, crowded and waiting, while one ruin shadows the center. I want to tend the stack again, pressing the tired corner down on the fat dot while the card hums steady. If the air pushes, I will lean harder against it, swapping another curve for a flat edge to catch the slip while the house waits.

action.why: The card hums warm and the stack still feels tired; I need to press down again to make sure the lean holds.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I am still new and not good at corners yet."
Something you no longer remember: "I drew the dot fat to match the swelling memory."

You drew "The First Square": A square around the dot. Four sides, made of thin lines. I am not good at corners. It will probably look lopsided, leaning to the right because I am new and unsteady. It is a box…
